meta.title: Two Ways to Grow
meta.skill_frame: Author's craft: read how the writer uses contrast to show the difference between two kinds of wood.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured part_1 100w at FK 5.1, part_2 108w at FK 4.7, part_3 106w at FK 4.8. The load is the contrast between two wood arrangements, the plant examples, and the position of the hard wood.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.basis: Adapted from Asa Gray, The Elements of Botany, For Beginners and For Schools (1887), under DESIGN_RULES 2.5.
source.attribution: Asa Gray. The Elements of Botany, For Beginners and For Schools. 1887. Project Gutenberg eBook #33757, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/33757, accessed 2026-11-11. Public domain in the United States.
source.adaptation: Split the passage and simplified the technical terms (parenchyma, exogenous and endogenous, monocotyl) into plain words; kept the two arrangements, the examples, and the hard-wood position; no facts added.
source.survey: Gray explains that stems build wood in two different patterns, and names a plant for each: an asparagus shoot and a corn stalk for one, a bean stalk and a maple for the other.
source.drafted_by: LessonBot harness (DeepSeek 1017), adapted from the human source; source review completed

session.difficulty_basis: contrast between two wood arrangements, examples, and the position of the hard wood

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: Wood begins to form in a stem while the plant is still young. It is arranged in one of two ways. In the first arrangement, the wood grows as separate threads scattered throughout the stem. In the second, the wood collects in a layer. If you cut the stem across, that layer appears as a ring between the soft center, called the pith, and the outer bark. The difference is visible in small plants, but it is even clearer in the stems of shrubs and trees that live for many years. Wood is made of wood cells and small tubes.
passage.part_2: Corn stalks and asparagus shoots show the first arrangement. A rattan shows it too. Plants with one seed leaf have this kind of stem. A bean stalk and the stem of a common tree show the second arrangement. Plants with more than one seed leaf have that kind. This kind has been called "inside-growing," though not very accurately. The second kind has been called "outside-growing," and that name is accurate enough. Palms and dragon trees show the first kind at their largest. Some yuccas grow as trees along the warm southern edge of the United States. The first kind reaches its greatest size in warm climates.
passage.part_3: In the first kind, the woody threads are crowded toward the outside of the stem, so the harder wood is on the outside. In the second kind, the oldest and hardest wood is at the center. The first kind has no clear separation of pith, bark, and wood into rings. It has no annual layers, and its bark does not peel off clean. A cut across the first stem shows threads, not a ring. Old yuccas do form a kind of layer and a scaly bark, and their woody threads curve, taper, and disappear at the rind. A cut across the second stem shows a ring.

items.prompt: What are the two ways wood can be arranged in a stem?

tutor_only.confirm: It can grow as separate threads scattered through the stem, or as a layer that looks like a ring.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says wood is arranged in two ways: separate threads throughout the stem, or a layer that appears as a ring in a cut stem.
tutor_only.tell: Wood can grow as separate threads through the stem. It can also grow as a layer that looks like a ring.
help: Find the sentence that begins 'It is arranged in one of two ways.'
tutor_only.core_idea: Wood has two arrangements: scattered threads or a ring-like layer.
accept_ideas: Separate threads scattered through the stem.
A layer that looks like a ring.
Scattered threads or a ring.
One kind has threads; the other has a ring.
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.ask: What is the other way wood can be arranged?

items.prompt: What do a corn stalk and a bean stalk show about the two kinds of wood?

tutor_only.confirm: The corn stalk shows the first kind, with scattered threads. The bean stalk shows the second kind, with a ring.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage names a corn stalk as an example of the first kind and a bean stalk as an example of the second kind.
tutor_only.tell: A corn stalk shows the first kind, with threads. A bean stalk shows the second kind, with a ring.
help: Find the corn stalk and the bean stalk in the middle of the passage.
Notice which kind each one shows.
tutor_only.core_idea: The corn stalk shows scattered threads; the bean stalk shows a ring.
accept_ideas: Corn shows the first kind and beans show the second.
The corn stalk has scattered threads.
The bean stalk has a ring.
They are examples of the two different kinds.
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: They say both plants show the same kind.
if_they_say.ask: Which plant shows scattered threads, and which shows a ring?

items.prompt: A grower cuts a stem and sees threads, no ring, and bark that will not peel cleanly. Which kind of wood is it, and what will that stem never show?

tutor_only.confirm: The first kind; it will never show annual layers, and its hard wood sits at the outside.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says plants with one seed leaf belong to the first kind and plants with more than one seed leaf belong to the second.
tutor_only.tell: Threads and no ring mean the first kind. It has no annual layers, and its hard wood is on the outside.
help: Find the sentence about one seed leaf.
Notice what kind of wood goes with more than one seed leaf.
tutor_only.core_idea: The first kind has scattered threads, no annual layers, and hard wood on the outside.
accept_ideas: The first kind. It will never show annual layers.
The kind with scattered threads; it has no annual layers.
The first kind, with hard wood on the outside and no annual layers.
The inside-growing kind; it has no annual layers.
not_required: Explaining what a seed leaf is
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: They say it is the second kind.
if_they_say.ask: Which kind has scattered threads and no annual layers?

items.prompt: The writer sets 'separate threads' against 'a layer.' What does that contrast let a reader picture?

tutor_only.confirm: The inside of the stem — threads scattered through it, or one ring — without a drawing.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The contrast sets 'separate threads' against 'a layer' so the reader can picture the inside of the stem without a drawing.
tutor_only.tell: The contrast turns the inside of the stem into a picture. You can see threads scattered through it, or one ring.
help: Find the sentence with 'separate threads' and 'layer.'
Notice what each pattern looks like in a cut stem.
tutor_only.core_idea: The contrast lets the reader picture the inside of the stem: scattered threads or one ring, without a drawing.
accept_ideas: The inside of the stem.
Threads scattered through the stem, or one ring.
What the two kinds look like inside.
A picture of the two patterns without a drawing.

if_they_say.when: They say the contrast tells which kind is better.
if_they_say.ask: What does the contrast let you picture inside the stem?

items.prompt: The opening sorts wood into two kinds. What does the last part do with each kind?

tutor_only.confirm: It shows where the hard wood sits and what each kind has or lacks.
tutor_only.correct_reason: Part_1 names the two arrangements; part_3 explains where the hard wood sits and how the two kinds differ in layers and bark.
tutor_only.tell: The opening names the two kinds. The last part shows where the hard wood sits and what each kind has or lacks.
help: Compare what the opening explains with what the last part explains.
Notice the move from the two arrangements to the hard wood.
tutor_only.core_idea: Part_1 names the two kinds; the last part shows where the hard wood sits and what each kind has or lacks.
accept_ideas: It shows where the hard wood sits in each kind.
